title: TPatch enumeration: 41 non-quad faces (18 triangles, 6+ pentagons) on Hand-30k
description:
Surfaced during PATCH-68 testing. After planar-graph face enumeration on Hand-30k T-mesh (332 arcs):
- 80 face cycles walked.
- side-count histogram: [-, -, 2-side: 4, 3-side: 18, 4-side: 39, 5-side: 3, 6-side: 4, 7-side: 1, 9-side: 1, 10-side: 3, 11-side: 1, 12-side: 1, 14-side: 1].
- 39 emitted as TPatches (4-corner quads).
- 41 skipped (non-quad).

Metriko presumably has more 4-corner Tquads. The 18 triangles are likely faces around singularities where the cardinal-direction transition rule miscounts corners (singularity vertices don't have a clean 4-quadrant tiling).

Fix candidates:
1. Better corner detection: use surface-tangent angle change > threshold instead of strict cardinal-mismatch.
2. T-junction recognition: side continuations across multi-arc with same cardinal should fold the 'extra' corners away.
3. Singularity-aware enumeration: at cone singularities, expect K corners where K matches the cone valence.

Downstream: extra correct patches scale linearly with output quad count.
definition-of-done: TPatchEnumerator emits >= 80% of face cycles as 4-corner TPatches on Hand-30k (= >64 of 80). Existing toy tests still pass.
testing-plan: 1. Inspect specific triangle faces — are they around singularities (3-valent vertices)? 2. Inspect pentagon faces — are they T-junctions? 3. Adjust corner detection accordingly.
